turns.text: ok wait quick q. im working all day today till closing (halloween) and want to draw skeleton latte art. how do i make a clean skeleton with etching tools

Fun plan! A skeleton face is the easiest version to keep clean. Here's a simple approach:

- Base: pour a full cup of latte with a flat, even white canvas of microfoam. Skip any rosetta or heart; you want a blank surface.
- Dark layer: pour the white foam as a solid circle, and leave a thin brown crema ring around the edge.
- Etching: use a toothpick or etching pen dipped in the dark crema or a little chocolate sauce.
  - Eyes: two oval sockets, filled in
  - Nose: small upside-down heart or triangle
  - Mouth: a straight line with short vertical teeth lines
- Tip: wipe the tool between each feature so the lines stay sharp.

Want the pour timing too?
yes pls. and how long to pour so it holds thru the rush. i just got past rosettas so my pour is pretty steady now

Nice, a steady pour is exactly what fine etching needs. Timing:

- Pour: about 8-10 seconds total. Start high and thin to build the crema, then lower the pitcher and push the foam in to make a solid white circle.
- Foam: slightly less stretched than for a rosetta. Tight, glossy microfoam with no big bubbles holds longest.
- Etch right away: you have roughly 30-60 seconds before the foam starts to separate and lines blur.
- Rush strategy: pour several cups, then etch them in a batch only if they sit under a minute. Otherwise do one at a time. Keep sauce pre-loaded in a small squeeze bottle so you aren't hunting for it.
- Serve fast: the drink is best handed over within a couple of minutes.

Practice one or two on a slow cup first.
